registration-for-a-campus-tour.title: Registration for a Campus Tour
registration-for-a-campus-tour.html:
Registration for a Campus Tour

We invite you to join us for a campus visit at A.C. Patil College of Engineering. The visit includes a half an hour information session with an admissions officer / admission counsellor and half an hour current undergraduate students, followed by a half an hour campus tour led by a current student.

Campus Tour Highlights:

Session on A.C. Patil College of Engineering’s Undergraduate Programmes:
Learn about the wide range of undergraduate programs offered at A.C. Patil College of Engineering. Get in-depth knowledge about the curriculum, specializations, faculty, and the opportunities available to students. Whether you’re interested in Electrical, Mechanical, Electronics & telecommunication, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Artificial Intelligence & Data Science, Computer Science Internet of things (IoT), Bachelor of Management Studies, Masters in Management Studies or any other discipline, this session will provide valuable insights into our academic environment and resources.

Tour of Classrooms, Auditorium, and Library:
Experience our modern classrooms equipped with the latest technology to enhance your learning experience. You’ll also visit our spacious and well-equipped auditorium where various academic and extracurricular events are held. Additionally, take a tour of our expansive library, home to a vast collection of books, journals, and digital resources, designed to support students in their academic endeavors.

Explore State-of-the-Art Indoor and Outdoor Sports Facilities:
A.C. Patil College of Engineering is proud of its excellent sports facilities. Whether you’re an athlete or just enjoy recreational activities, you’ll have the opportunity to explore both indoor and outdoor sports arenas. Our facilities include well-maintained courts, gymnasiums, and fields, all designed to promote a healthy and active lifestyle.

Schedule: Monday to Friday
Timings: 9:30 AM – 1:30 PM, 2:00 PM – 5:00 PM

For campus tours on Saturdays, Sundays, or public holidays, please contact Dr. Vishal B. Patil at +91 9892648707.

Please choose an available date from the calendar below to sign up, then fill out the registration form. After completing your registration, we will contact you via WhatsApp, phone, or email with useful details to help you prepare for your visit and send you reminders.

institute-innovation-cell-incubation-cen.title: Institute Innovation Cell Incubation Center
institute-innovation-cell-incubation-cen.html:
Institute Innovation Cell

ACPCE Innovation Cell

  • Innovation Cell of the institute is formed  to encourage, inspire and nurture students  with an innovative bent of mind. A talent hunt is conducted to select team members. Students from multidisciplinary background form a team. A culture of working in groups and problem solving is developed. They are trained, assigned task and motivated to work on their ideas and share their view points
  • Students are also encourage for startup ideas.  The aim is to develop a network and support system, so that the prototype can be transformed to realistic and successful product. They will be ready for their own startup and take up the challenges of the real world
  • The students groomed in I-Cell are encouraged to participate various university level, state level, national level  and other project competition.
  • ACPCE  Innovation Cell is established  to Cultivate  the culture of Innovation among the students .
  • The aim is to encourage, inspire and nurture  students by supporting them to work with new ideas and transform them into prototypes  to serve the society and with their own development.
  • There are around 30 students and 7 faculties from different disciplines   working in the Innovation cell. 
  • The ideas are being transform into realistic project with  contribution from multidisciplinary approach

Functions

  • To organize Seminar and workshops 
  • Interaction with  innovators & Entrepreneur
  • Creating a network  to  help  incubation
  • To encourage the students to participate in different Idea / project/ Challenges Competition.
  • To showcase the  Idea/ prototype of faculty and students

Vision & Mission

Vision

Empowering tomorrow’s innovators, ACPCE Innovation Cell envisions a vibrant ecosystem where students, faculty, and multidisciplinary teams collaboratively conceive, develop, and transform ideas into impactful solutions that serve society and foster individual growth. We aspire to be a catalyst for innovation, encouraging students to create a lasting impact on the world through their entrepreneurial journey.

Mission

Our mission at ACPCE Innovation Cell is to cultivate an innovation-driven culture among students. We are dedicated to:

  • Encouraging, inspiring, and nurturing students, fostering their innovative mindset.
  • Providing a platform for students and faculty from diverse backgrounds to collaborate and work on innovative projects.
  • Transforming ideas into realistic projects through multidisciplinary approaches.
  • Organizing seminars, workshops, and facilitating interactions with innovators and entrepreneurs.
  • Building a supportive network for incubation and growth.
  • Motivating and guiding students on their journey from ideation to entrepreneurship.
  • Encouraging active participation in various idea, project, and challenge competitions.
  • Showcasing faculty and student ideas and prototypes that contribute to positive change." Through these endeavors, we aim to prepare our students for the dynamic challenges of the real world and inspire them to become successful innovators and entrepreneurs.

Objectives & Outcomes

Program Educational Objectives(PEOs)

After successful completion of the program, the graduates will be able-

PEO 1 : To equip students with essential managerial skills and provide a strong foundation in key business areas such as finance, marketing and human resources.

PEO 2 : To instill an understanding of ethical considerations and sustainable practices in management, including institutional social responsibility.

PEO3 : To develop effective oral and written communication skills and support entrepreneurial thinking and innovation through research, internships, projects, and encourage continuous professional and cognitive development.

Program Specific Outcomes(PSOs)

PSO 1 : Create Skilled Professionals who will critically analyse, strategies ,innovate, decide ,control and evaluate in complex business world.

PSO 2 : Exhibit proficiency through managerial, research bend of mind , social behavior and bring about a holistic development in students.

Program Outcomes(POs)

Engineering knowledge :

Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified

in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering Problems.

Problem Analysis : Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

Design/Development Solutions : Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

Conduct investigations of complex problems : Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

Modern tool usage : Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

The engineer and society : Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

Environment and sustainability : Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.

Ethics : Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

Individual and team work : Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

Communication : Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.

Project management and finance : Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

Life-long learning : Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

Our Vision & Mission

Our Vision

To create skilled managerial professionals for catering the needs of industries and society.

Our Mission

  • To provide innovative and student friendly qualified faculties and required infrastructure for disseminating quality education which inculcates steady learning attitudes and intentions.
  • To provide platform for bridging the gap between industry-academia interactions through various business related and entrepreneurial activities.
  • To instill social values and responsible attitude towards mankind and society amongst students through various extracurricular and socially derived activities.

Message From HOD

Dear BMS Students,

Welcome to the inaugural batch of the Bachelor of Management Studies at C. Patil College of Engineering, Navi Mumbai. As we embark on this new journey together, I want to inspire you to embrace the opportunities and challenges ahead with enthusiasm and integrity. Our department is built on a foundation of excellence, innovation, and ethical leadership. You will find that our curriculum is designed to not only equip you with the skills needed for a successful career in management but also to instill the values of responsibility and ethical decision-making. This is your chance to shape the future of our program and leave a lasting impact. Engage actively in your studies, collaborate with your peers, and seek out every opportunity for growth. Your dedication and passion will define your success and help us build a legacy of excellence. Welcome aboard, and I look forward to seeing all that we will achieve together.

Dr. N. Mahesh

MBA (Marketing & System), LL.B, Ph.D (Business Administration)

student-activitiesart.title: Student Activitiesart
student-activitiesart.html:
Department of Artificial Intelligence & Data Science

Student Activities

Presentation on Startup Business Ideas Startup Business Ideas

A Presentation on Startup Business Ideas was organized by the Departments of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science and Computer Science on 03 November 2025, with the participation of 42 students, conducted from 10:00 PM to 1:30 PM. The activity showcased a wide range of handmade startup products developed by students, including eco-friendly crafts and home décor made from upcycled materials, customized accessories and crochet jewelry, gourmet baked goods and healthy snacks such as handmade peanut butter, and handmade stationery and personalized gifts like printed T-shirts and phone cases. Each team delivered a 7–8 minute business pitch explaining their product or service, team responsibilities, vision and mission, target audience, digital marketing strategies, financial summary, and lessons learned. The presentations were evaluated based on clarity and delivery (30%), product viability and innovation (30%), financial accuracy (20%), and response to Q&A (20%). The activity provided students with valuable exposure to startup planning, digital marketing strategies, and financial analysis, enabling them to translate their creativity and innovation into practical, real-world business applications.

Workshop on Software Testing

The Software Testing Workshop conducted on 1st October 2025 for students of the AI & DS Department, under the guidance of Prof. Vandana Sonawane, provided a structured introduction to the fundamentals of software testing and its significance in the software development lifecycle. The session covered essential theoretical concepts, including testing types, methodologies, and quality assurance practices, followed by a hands-on demonstration of the Eclipse IDE. Students were guided through test case creation, bug identification, debugging techniques, and test result analysis. The workshop effectively strengthened students’ foundational knowledge, enhanced their practical testing skills, and prepared them to apply systematic testing approaches in academic and industry-related projects.

Smart India Hackathon: Institute-Level Screening

The Smart India Hackathon – Internal Rounds, held on 26th September 2025 with participation from 150+ students across all departments, began with the felicitation of Principal Dr. Vijaykumar N. Pawar, followed by inspiring addresses from him and AI & DS HOD Prof. Shilpali P. Bansu, highlighting the importance of innovation and problem-solving. The event progressed into parallel evaluation rounds where student teams presented prototypes and solutions to faculty panels, gaining hands-on experience in pitching ideas, refining concepts, and working under structured guidelines. The internal hackathon fostered creativity, teamwork, and technical excellence, helping identify strong teams for higher SIH levels while motivating students to approach real-world challenges with confidence and innovation.

Industrial Visit

The Industrial Visit to Reliance Jio, RCP Park Ghansoli, conducted on 15th September 2025 for AI & DS students, provided valuable industry exposure to advanced communication technologies and telecom infrastructure. Students experienced Jio’s True 5G demonstrations and learned about its applications across sectors such as agriculture, automobiles, healthcare, and education. They also gained practical insights into pole-level network operations and fibre technology through sessions led by Mr. Saurabh Srivastava and Ms. Abhilasha Lawangkar Surve, with overall guidance from Mr. Manish Athalye. The visit strengthened the link between theoretical learning and real-world systems, enhanced students’ understanding of modern telecom networks, and encouraged them to explore careers in advanced communication and digital infrastructure.

Blueprint to be a successful engineer

The Blueprint to Be a Successful Engineer session held on 19th September 2025 for AI & DS students, delivered by Mr. Raghvan Koli, focused on developing smarter study habits and cultivating a strong mindset for long-term success. The speaker emphasized techniques such as active recall, spaced repetition, and focused learning, along with the importance of goal-setting, discipline, consistency, and effective time management. Through practical guidance and real-life examples, the session motivated students to adopt productive habits, stay determined, and work consistently toward academic and personal excellence.

Engineer’s Day

The Engineers’ Day Celebration on 15th September 2025 brought together AI & DS students to honour the contributions of engineers and promote innovative thinking. The event began with an inaugural address and an inspiring message from HOD Prof. Shilpali P. Bansu, followed by poster presentations and quiz competitions that encouraged creativity, technical skills, and healthy competition. The celebration fostered teamwork, analytical thinking, and professional motivation, inspiring students to value the engineering profession and strive for excellence.

Teacher’s Day

The Teacher’s Day Celebration held on 15th September 2025 brought together AI & DS students to honour and appreciate the dedication and contributions of their teachers. The program began with an inaugural speech highlighting the significance of the day, followed by an inspiring address from HOD Prof. Shilpali P. Bansu on the noble role of educators. A cake-cutting ceremony and the distribution of small gifts to faculty members symbolized the students’ gratitude, respect, and affection. The event strengthened the student–teacher bond, fostering a deeper sense of appreciation among students and reaffirming the lasting impact of teachers in shaping knowledge, character, and future success.

Orientation Program for Hack The Code Hackathon

The Hack The Core Hackathon Announcement held on 10th September 2025 for 60+ AI & DS students provided a comprehensive overview of the upcoming November 15–16 hackathon. The resource person explained the event structure, rules, domains, problem statements, evaluation criteria, and submission guidelines, ensuring students were well-prepared in advance. The session emphasized innovation, teamwork, and time management, motivating participants to begin ideating early and plan responsibilities effectively. Overall, it boosted clarity, confidence, and excitement among students, leading to greater readiness and increased participation for the hackathon.

Awareness Program on Waste Management (NEP Activity)

The Awareness Program on Waste Management held on 9th September 2025, led by social worker Ms. Merietta Pallissery, engaged 120+ students from the AI & DS and Computer departments. The session highlighted the importance of sustainable waste management, focusing on waste types, harmful effects of improper disposal, and practical methods such as segregation, recycling, and composting. Students learned about the 3Rs along with extended concepts like Refuse, Recover, and Redesign, and gained insights into the impactful work of organizations like Stree Mukti Sanghatana and Parisar Sakhi Vikas Sanstha. Through real-world examples and environmental data, the program emphasized collective responsibility, community participation, and the role of waste management in building zero-waste and sustainable cities, inspiring students to adopt eco-friendly practices and contribute to a cleaner and greener future.

Career Guidance and Opportunities for Higher Studies AbroadHigher Studies Abroad2024

The Department of AI & DS conducted a seminar titled “Career Guidance and Opportunities for Higher Studies Abroad” on 30th July 2025, delivered by alumnus Mr. Chirag Naresh Patil. With the participation of 100+ students, the session provided insights into higher education options in countries like the USA, UK, Canada, Germany, and Australia, along with the importance of exams such as GRE, TOEFL, IELTS, and GMAT. Mr. Patil also explained financial planning, scholarships, part-time work, and education loans, while offering a clear roadmap covering university shortlisting, test preparation, profile building, SOPs, recommendation letters, and visa processes. The interactive session helped students understand global opportunities in AI & DS and equipped them with essential guidance for planning their higher studies and career paths.

Seminar on “Abroad Studies with Scholarships

The Artificial Intelligence & Data Science department organized a Seminar about Abroad Studies with Scholarships on 1st October 2024. The resource person was Mr. Suraj Choudhar, Next Step. He introduced students with the information that many deemed universities abroad (US, UK, Ireland, Zurich, and so on) give scholarships to students that help to pursue their Masters with Zero to 70-80% discounted tuition fees. The speaker discussed the Tuition fees of various esteemed Universities. He also cleared myths about life during Masters abroad. He motivated a lot of students in pursuing Masters abroad with zero to minimal fees.

Seminar on Guidelines & Strategies for SIH 2024

Guidelines & Strategies for SIH 2024 Seminar was organized by SHAIDS (Student Hub of AI & DS) on 10 th September 2024. The resource Person was Mr. Ali Mustufa, Senior Developer Advocate at Postman. He delivered a detailed presentation on participating in the Smart India Hackathon (SIH). He guided participants through SIH ideas, strategies for choosing topics with minimal submissions, and the importance of focusing on basic concepts and iterating on features. Mr. Mustufa also offered practical advice on creating effective PowerPoint presentations and forming ideal teams.

Teachers Day Celebration

On 5th September 2024, CSI committee of Artificial Intelligence and Data Science organized Teachers Day Celebration. The event began with warm welcome and hurtful appreciation session where students took time to express their gratitude for guidance, support and wisdom that the teachers have continuously provided.

Group Discussion Competition

The CSI student council of the AI & DS department had organized a Group Discussion Competition for students to enhance communication, critical thinking and problem solving skills, fostering collaboration innovation and Productivity. Students learned how to engage in group discussions and articulate their ideas to distinguish them from other members. The competition boosted Students self-confidence, enabling them to express their viewpoints more assertively in group settings.

Seminar on UI/UX Design

The Artificial Intelligence & Data Science department organized a Seminar on UI/UX design on 14 August 2024. The speaker was Mr. Abhishek Kashid, CEO and Cofounder of Paux Academy and Alumni of A.C Patil College of Engineering. He explained in detail about UI/UX covering topics like practical knowledge, its components, and architecture. Furthermore, he also discussed the evolving role of AI in design and provided valuable insights for newcomers on how to enter this field. He also speaks about the latest technologies through engaging and interactive sessions.Students gained a clear understanding of the fundamental principles and practical applications of product UI/UX design.The session encouraged students to embrace creativity and innovation in their design work.

Seminar on How to Plan for Start-Up & Legal Ethical Steps

How to Plan for Start-Up & Legal, Ethical Steps seminar was organized by our AI & DS department on 09 August 2024. Resource Persons for this seminar are Mr Nohid Chougle, partner at Quaestio LLP and CA Mr Darpan Juthani, Advisory at The Quaestio and Proprietor at Darpan Juthani & Co. They discussed the crucial financial processes involved in launching a new startup and He provided insights into the necessary steps for registering a company and elaborated on the formation of private companies. Finally they conclude the topic by elaborating the importance of scalability planning, offering strategies for sustainable growth in the start-ups.Students gained a comprehensive understanding of the financial processes crucial for launching a start-up, including company registration and the formation of private companies.

Project Competition

Project competition was organized by Jawahar Education Society’s A. C. Patil College of Engineering, Department of AI & DS on April 18, 2024. Students got a platform to present their working Project model. Participation certificates were awarded for every participant.

Workshop on Developing Desktop Applications with API in Python

CSI student council AI & DS department had organized a two day workshop “Developing Desktop Applications with API in Python” 14th & 15th February 2024. Mr.Yash Chaudhary students of BE conducted the workshop. From basics to various desktop applications were covered in the session. More than 40+ students gained knowledge from this workshop.

Seminar on AI & ML : Impact of AI on Jobs and Current Industry Trends

Seminar based on AI & ML was organized by our AI & DS department on 31st January 2024. Speakers of this seminar(from Expertrons).1. Mr. Milan Mapara 2.Mr. Pranit Singh. Focused on Generative AI & Current Industry Trends. Speaker spoke about The widespread adoption of Generative AI could disrupt industries reliant on creative workforces, such as graphic design, writing, and music composition. It may lead to job displacement in these sectors while also creating new opportunities in AI-related fields. Organization offered different Internship opportunities to the students.

Debate Competition

CSI student council AI & DS department had organized a debate competition on 26 October 2023 for Students to generate effective critical thinking into primary issues in the given topic. Students got exposure to expand their understanding in the given topic. Students got effective thinking, while they considered others’ perspectives. Students got confidence in their own answers and evidence.

Workshop on Deep Learning using Matlab

One day hands on workshop delivered by Kunal Khandelwal (From MathWorks). The objective of the workshop was to understand the basics of Deep Learning. Students are able to create an image classification network from scratch. Created & trained deep learning networks using Deep Network Designer network App. Students learnt all the applications of Deep learning. CSI student council AI & DS department had organized a debate competition on 26 October 2023 for Students to generate effective critical thinking into primary issues in the given topic. Students got exposure to expand their understanding in the given topic. Students got effective thinking, while they considered others’ perspectives. Students got confidence in their own answers and evidence.

Seminar on NPTEL Awareness

Seminar conducted on NPTEL Awareness on 12 th September 2023 by Dr. Dipti Patil to explore various courses on nptel to enhance their knowledge and implement new ideas for society. Speaker spoke about the subjects being taught by qualified professors and later getting certified by IIT and IISC.

Seminar on Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning

Seminar organized on AI & ML by Kongsberg Maritime India on 08 September 2023.Seminar delivered by Mr. Darren Murphy – Sr. Vice President Technology Automation & Control Leadership / Chairman of Board – KM India , Mr. Nirav Kavishwer – Director – Software Projects & IT Management – KM India, Ms. Arti Shetty – Head HR & Admin – KM India. Speaker talked about the organization overview and their research area. They offered some internship opportunities to the students.

Competition on Start-up

A one day Start-Up competition was organized by Jawahar Education Society’s , A. C. Patil College Of Engineering, Department Of Computer Engineering in collaboration with the Artificial Intelligence and Data Science Department on August 29, 2023. Students got a platform to demonstrate their Start-Ups. They got an exposure to brand and venture concepts to a bigger audience. They established relationships with potential partners and customers.
Judegs Detail: It was judged by Dr. N. Mahesh (HOD, Department of MMS), Dr. Varsha Bhole (HOD, Department of Information Technology), Dr. A. R. Sonule (Associate Professor, Department of Computer Engineering) of A. C. Patil College Of Engineering.

Data Science Bootcamp

The 4-day bootcamp “Data Science” was conducted by the CSI student council of the AI & DS department. The resource persons are Prof. Amol Patil, Ms. Jyotsana Parkhedkar, Ms. Khushi Singh, Mr. Yash Shrisath delivers the fundamentals to present Data Science techniques hands-on. The workshop equipped participants with a solid understanding of linear algebra’s significance in data science and provided them with the tools necessary to apply these concepts effectively in their respective domains. Participants gained familiarity with Power BI Desktop, exploring its interface, data importing options, and basic functionalities. Power BI workshop provided with practical skills and insights to leverage the tool effectively for data analysis and visualization tasks

Seminar on Unlocking Opportunities with Northeastern University Global campus

Seminar “Unlocking Opportunities with Northeastern University Global campus”was organized by the CSI Committee of AI & DS department conducted by Our Speaker Ms. Debopriya Bhattacharya. Northern University provided a comprehensive overview of the institution’s academic prowess, research excellence, vibrant student life, and commitment to societal impact. Attendees left with a deeper understanding of the university’s values and contributions to the educational landscape.

Competition on Business Plan

A one day “Business Plan” competition was organized by Jawahar Education Society’s , A. C. Patil College Of Engineering, Department Of Computer Engineering in collaboration with Artificial Intelligence and Data Science Department on July 31, 2023. Students got a platform to share their business plans in different domains.
Judegs Detail: It was judged by Dr. M. M. Deshpande (HOD, Department of Computer Engineering), Dr. D. S. Marathe (HOD, Department of EXTC Engineering), Dr. Anupama Singh (Department of Electrical Engineering) of A. C. Patil College Of Engineering.

Workshop on IPR and Patenting

The Artificial Intelligence Data Science Department in association with IIC and CSI had organized a one day workshop on “IPR and Patenting” for students and faculties on 26th July, 2023. The speaker of the workshop was Dr. Asha Durafe Assistant Professor, Cyber Security Department, Shah & Anchor Kutchhi Engineering College, Mumbai. It was a very interactive session in which our students and faculties gained knowledge regarding Intellectual Property Rights and Patenting.

Seminar on Artificial Intelligence & Machine learning

A one day seminar was conducted on “Artificial Intelligence & Machine learning” organized by Jawahar Education Society’s , A. C. Patil College Of Engineering, Department Of Computer Engineering in collaboration with Artificial Intelligence and Data Science Department Monday, February 27, 2023, at 11 a.m. Students got an understanding about concepts like how to create machines that can think like humans, or at least mimic human behavior in some way. ALso how to build systems that can learn from historical data, identify patterns, and make logical decisions with little to no human intervention.

Instructor Detail: It was conducted by Dr. Pooja Raundale, Sardar Patel Institute of Technology, Andheri (W), Mumbai.

Project and paper presentation competition “TECHTATVA 2023”

A project and paper presentation competition “TECHTATVA 2023” was organized under MESA on 18th and 19th April 2023. The event was well synchronized under the leadership of MESA team members headed by Mechanical Faculties Dr. L. K. Pandey , Prof. Ruchita Shrimali and Prof. A. A. Mate.. Participation certificates were given to each participants and prize money was given to the winners.

Seminar on Career Counseling

The department of Mechanical Engineering had organized a career counseling seminar on 18.01.2023. The seminar helped students in gaining clarity on career goals, identifying job market trends, evaluating one’s skills and competencies, gaining knowledge about various industries, and exploring different career paths.

Chhatrapati Shivaji Mahavarj Jayanti

Shivaji Jayanti is celebrated every year in February to honor the great Maratha emperor. Shivaji Jayanti is celebrated on February 19 every year in honor of the founder of the Maratha Kingdom.

Gandhi Jayanti

Mahatma Gandhi’s birthday (Gandhi Jayanti or Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti) . It marks the anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi’s birth on October 2, 1869. Gandhi is remembered for his contributions towards the Indian freedom struggle.

Daughter’s Day

On account of the Daughter’s day which is celebrated on 22nd September every year MECHANICAL ENGNEERING STUDENT’S ASSOCIATION (M.E.S.A) organized an event on 1st October 2019. The main part of the event was street play.

Aaroha

MESA under itself conducts a departmental festival called “AAROHA” every year. It consists of a technical event, a non-technical event and a social event. This year we hosted an event called “RC racing” which was held for the Second time in Navi Mumbai last year. The event was held in the month of Feb 2018.

Piping Engineering Course

Value added course on Piping Engineering was coordinated by Dr. S. S. Pawar. Course was held for six hours on each Saturday, from 19th Aug 2017 to 30th Dec 2017. Dr. B. A. Mujawar (Director of Zero liquid Discharge- ZLD Solution Panel) conducted the course for 18 mechanical students of third year and final year on nine Saturdays. The industrial visit was also organised at Panvel MIDC on 30.12.2017 by Dr. B. A. Mujawar.

Avishkar Research Convection

Institute level Avishkar research convection 2017-2018 was organised on 22-12-2017 by Dr. S. S. Pawar (HOD of Mechanical Department). Dr. V. N. Pawar (HOD of Extc department), Dr. M. N. Deshpande (HOD of Comp department) and Dr. Sachin Kamble did the judging of the event. This activity was coordinated by Prof. (Mrs.) Sonal Patil from Electronics. Total six best groups from UG level were selected for district round. Two groups were selected for University round from Mechanical and Computer Department.

Engineering's Day

On 15th September 2017 we had invited 2 guest lecturers who provided us with valuable information. Prof N. Mahesh enlightened us about the ‘Role of an engineer as a manager’. Prof. V. S . Patil gave talk on ‘Power scenario in India’.

Mesh Runner

MESH RUNNER was organised by Mechanical department students in 2017. It was the competition which included manufacturing of bots and designing mesh. Two teams were opposing each other in this contest.

com-student-activities.title: Com Student Activities
com-student-activities.html:
Department of Computer Engineering

Student Activities

Docker Seminar

A one day webinar was conducted on “DOCKERS : APPLICATION DEVELOPMENT TOOL” organized by JAWAHAR EDUCATION SOCIETY’S , A. C. PATIL COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING, DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTER ENGINEERING. on May 31,2020 at 03:30 pm to 5:30 pm. Instructor Details: It was conducted by Mr. Suresh Gupta Senior Full Stack Developer (F-Secure, Finland) AWS Solutions Architect Certified,API development, API management, Building microservices and UI, DevOps, AWS, Azure cloud, IoT Mode of conduction: There were two modes of conduction: Google Meet Youtube Live It was conducted by our respected faculty members : Mrs. S. P. Bansu, Mrs. R. Y. Patil and Mrs. S. R. Chunamari and CSI members Hitesh chaudhari(President of CSI), Jayesh pawar(Vice- President of CSI), Samruddhi chavan(Secretary) of the Computer Department .

Technovent 2019-2020

Project and Poster Competition

Teachers Day and Engineers Day Celebration 2019-2020

Workshop on Web Development

Web development is the creation of dynamic web applications. The web development process includes web design, web content development, client-side/server-side scripting and network security configuration etc. Introductory one day workshop on Web Development was organized by Prof. Shilpali Bansu of Computer Department of ACPCE on October 5, 2017. The workshop was attended by the students of all departments. She also shared simple guidelines which help users to make your own website.

Seminar on Exploring Identity (Higher Study)

Computer Department organized one day seminar on Exploring Identity on September 28, 2017 in our college. Mr. Vibhav Srivastava, the resource person from Made Easy Institute provided basic information about GATE, GRE,ESE exams for higher studies. The seminar was fruitful about the preparation of aptitude test of above exams.

Cleanliness Drive

Cleanliness is next to Godliness, following this statement, our Computer Department of ACPCE College, Kharghar has conducted ‘Cleanliness Drive’ on September 24, 2017. We have targeted core areas of Kharghar for cleaning. Being a responsible citizen our faculty members have enthusiastically participated in it.

Teacher’s day & Engineer’s Day

Students of our department celebrated Teacher’s day and Engineer’s Day on September 15, 2017 to pay the tribute to the greatest Indian Engineer Bharat Ratna Mokshagundam Visvesvaraya.

Seminar on Skill Development in Tosca given by Mrs. Bela Joshi (Seed Infotech Ltd.) on 10th October 2017

Mechnical Talk on Next Generation Telecommunication Networking & Job Opportunities given by Dr. Munir Sayyad (Reliance Jio) on 28th October 2017

com-student-association.title: Com Student Association
com-student-association.html:
Computer Society of India

Formed in 1965, the CSI has been instrumental in guiding the Indian IT industry down the right path since its formative years. Today, the CSI has 70 chapters all over India, 358 student branches, and more than 90,000 members, including India’s most famous IT industry leaders, brilliant scientists and dedicated academicians. Now, you have the opportunity to be a part of this distinguished fraternity too. The mission of the CSI is to facilitate research, knowledge sharing, learning and career enhancement for all categories of IT professionals, while simultaneously inspiring and nurturing new entrants into the industry and helping them to integrate into the IT community. Computer Engineering Department has student association CSI-ACPCE active under CSI professional body. Various technical activities are organized for students under the banner of CSI-ACPCE to improve their skills.

Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering

Student Activities (SAeT)

International Women’s Day Celebration (08-03-2023)

Two of our ladies faculties Dr. Mrs Jaya Terdale and Prof. Ms. Anagha V. Malkapurkar were felicitated by Hon. HOD Dr. Mr. Dipak S. Marathe. BE, TE and SE Girls Students were felicitated by Prof. Nitin Chawande, Prof Pundlik Ghate and Prof. Sandeep Matey respectively by offering chocolates. To bring in the social responsibilities, respect and feeling of gratitude towards the women by citing students own mother’s example who stands behind each of them as a strong support was the center of discussion.

Gurupournima

Gurupournima is the first event of cultural team celebrated on 19/7/17 to honor and express gratitude to the Divine Master or Gurus. On this auspicious day, posts of cultural core and general committee members were rewarded by Hon. H.O.D, Dr V. N. Pawar. & Faculty Committee Members.
University Organized Youth Festival – 2017 ( VII Raigad Zone – Intercollegiate Competition) University of Mumbai, Department of Student’s development organized 50th Golden Jubilee inter – Collegiate zonal youth festival : Zone VII – Raigad North in Karnatak Lingayat Society’s , KLE college of science and commerce, Kalambol on 8/8/17. Dr. V.N.Pawar (HOD- Extc) triggered the idea of active participation of our college students in Golden Jubilee year inter collegiate Youth festival – 2017. Our honorable Principal Dr. D. G. Borse granted the fees of registration for first chunk of students who responded to our first call for participation. Prof. S.W.Matey(EXTC), Prof. Mrs. Rashmi Mahajan (Extc), Prof. Mrs. Rupali Pande (Extc) , Prof. Ms. Bhagyashree Borse (Extc) encouraged the students for taking part in various activities. Indian classical instrumental solo (Taalwadya) Master. Omkar Badrike secured 1st rank at zonal level in 50th youth festival Mumbai University

Teacher’s & Engineer’s Day

On 5th September, Teachers Day is celebrated all over India, in the memory of Dr. Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan, former President of India SAeT celebrates Teachers Day, with both teacher’s and student’s active participation. Teacher’s day and Engineers day was celebrated at department of Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering on 15/9/ 2017, at Room No: 125, seminar hall by SAeT cultural committee.

Navratri Celebration

With an aim to spread joy and happiness; Department of Electronics and Telecommunication of AC Patil COE , Kharghar has organized Dandiya and Garba on 19/9/17. The campus looked like a mini Gujarat, with all the Students; dressed up in traditional Gujarati attire and dancing to the rhythmic Dandiya beats!

Electronics & Telecommunication Engineering

Student Activities (ISF)

Workshop on NodeMCU

Department of Electronics And Telecommunication and IETE students forum, organized a workshop on NodeMCU on 15th September, 2023. The workshop started at 10 am which had two sessions, one session for introduction to NodeMCU and second session for hands on practical on NodeMCU. Both the sessions was conducted by a third year student Mr. Abhishekkumar Lal. What is a NodeMCU and why it is used at such a large scale, why does everyone prefer NodeMCU, etc. was explained to the students. Then, the students were explained about the Architecture of NodeMCU, its hardware and what it provides us. Students were informed about all the minor components, all the input/output pins and ports present on the NodeMCU. All the hardware related concepts were explained in the first half session of the workshop. The second half of the workshop begins with introduction to Programming, as students of FE were also attending the workshop. After explaining all about the programming, the most important part begins

Workshop on PCB Making and Arduino

In this workshop we take Two sessions in 1st session we take workshop on Arduino, in Arduino workshop we introduce students with Arduino IDE software then we do hands-on with Arduino board interfacing with some sensors and output devices.
In 2nd session we take on PCB making, in that session we introduce students with “PCB Wizard” software that is use for PCB track designing. After that we give students brief information about PCB board and after that each group made their own PCB in guidance of workshop team.

tele-student-association.html:
IETE Students Forum(ISF)

The Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers (IETE) founded in 1953 is one of the leading Professional Society in India. In EXTC department, ISF (IETE Students Forum) was formed in 2003. ISF in association with EXTC department provides the platform for the students in research oriented work and under this various seminars and workshops are arranged in EXTC department of A. C. Patil College of Engineering. Benefits of this is the students can publish their papers in Journal of Education and can also attend IETE technical programs in India at reduced registration fees.

student-association-activities.title: Student Association Activities
student-association-activities.html:
Department of Electrical Engineering

Student Activities

SESSION ON CONSERVATION OF OIL & GAS – “GO GREEN”

The Engineering Students’ Association (EESA) organized a programme titled “Conservation of Oil & Gas – Go Green” under the banner of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) – Saksham Scheme on 06th February 2026 for B.E. Electrical Engineering students. The programme was conducted under the departmental course “Electrical System Design Management & Auditing (ESDM&A)” and under the guidance of Programme Co-ordinators Prof. P. B. Sutar and Prof. A. A. Kale. The session was delivered by Mr. Sambhaji N. Kadam, an expert speaker from Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL).

The session emphasized the importance of energy conservation, efficient utilization of oil and gas resources, and the responsibility of engineers in promoting sustainable practices. It provided practical insights into minimizing energy wastage and adopting effective energy management techniques, thereby enhancing students’ awareness and encouraging them to contribute towards sustainable development and responsible resource utilization.

Workshop on “Entrepreneurship and Innovation as a Career Opportunity”

A workshop on “Entrepreneurship and Innovation as a Career Opportunity” was organized for all engineering students on 5th February 2026. The workshop was conducted under the guidance of Ms. Sangita R Nandurkar and was led by expert Mr. B. R. Venkatesh &Mrs. Tejaswini

The main objective of the program was to motivate students and help them understand the process of entrepreneurship and the various career opportunities available in this field. The speaker elaborated on the key goals, essential elements, and advantages of entrepreneurship, encouraging students to consider innovation and startups as viable career options. The expert also shared valuable insights into the challenges and difficulties faced by successful innovators and entrepreneurs, providing students with practical knowledge and real-world perspectives. The session proved to be highly interactive and informative, enabling participants to gain a deeper understanding of the entrepreneurial journey.

A total of 155 students and 6 faculty members actively participated in the workshop, making the event highly successful.

Key Outcomes of the Event:

To motivate students towards innovation and startup policies

To help students learn from the challenges and difficulties faced by successful innovators

To understand the process of becoming an entrepreneur

The workshop successfully inspired students to explore entrepreneurship as a promising career path and enhanced their awareness of innovation-driven opportunities.

PERSONALITY & SKILL DEVELOPMENT SESSION – “UNLOCK YOUR PERSONALITY, UPGRADE YOUR SKILLS”

EESA organized a Personality & Skill Development Session titled “Unlock Your Personality, Upgrade Your Skills” for S.E., T.E., and B.E. Electrical Engineering students on 03rd February 2026.. The session was conducted by Mr. Sahil Shaikh, Founder of YuvaPrep and an expert speaker in personality development and skill enhancement.

The objective of the session was to help students enhance their communication skills, build self-confidence, develop professional behavior, and improve their overall personality. The session provided practical insights and guidance to support students in their academic growth and prepare them effectively for future career opportunities.

 

 

National Start up Day

The National Startup Day was organized for Electrical Engineering students on 03rd February 2026 with the objective of igniting the spirit of entrepreneurship among students. The event was conducted under the guidance of Ms. Sangita R. Nandurkar and was led by Mr. Sahil Shaikh (YUVAPREP, Mumbai).

The program aimed to create awareness among students and faculty about the startup ecosystem in India, including government initiatives, funding opportunities, and incubation support systems. The session also focused on promoting innovation and an entrepreneurial culture within the institution by encouraging idea generation, problem-solving abilities, and a risk-taking mindset.

The speaker highlighted the significant role of the Startup India Initiative in shaping and strengthening India’s startup ecosystem. Students were provided with complete insights into the process of starting a startup, including idea validation, planning, execution, and growth strategies. The session offered valuable real-world perspectives through interaction with entrepreneurs and startup mentors. The event proved to be highly informative and motivating, equipping students with practical knowledge and inspiration to explore entrepreneurship as a viable career path.

Key Outcomes of the Event:

Enhanced awareness about the startup ecosystem in India

Understanding of government schemes, funding opportunities, and incubation support

Motivation towards innovation and entrepreneurial thinking

Practical insights into startup planning and execution

seminar on “Upcoming Trends in Electrical Engineering in Private / Government Sector”

The Department of Electrical Engineering successfully organized a seminar on “Upcoming Trends in Electrical Engineering in Private / Government Sector” on 22nd January 2024. The seminar was conducted as part of the Training and Placement activities for undergraduate Electrical Engineering students, under the guidance of Prof. Surekha Mahadik.

The session was delivered by Mr. Shubham Kamble, Assistant Engineer at MahaTransco, who is also a proud alumnus of the department. He shared valuable insights into the latest developments and emerging trends in the field of electrical engineering, with a special focus on opportunities available in both the private and government sectors.

Mr. Kamble discussed real-world industrial practices, advancements in power systems, GIS substations, operation and maintenance challenges, and the essential skills required to succeed in the evolving electrical engineering landscape. He also guided students on career planning, preparation for competitive examinations, and emphasized the importance of technical knowledge, discipline, and continuous learning. The seminar was highly interactive and informative.   •  A Report on Industrial Visit at ± 500 KV HVDC, Padghe Maharashtra
  • Date : 02nd March 2023 & 03rd March 2023
  • Department : Electrical Engineering
  • Venue : HVDC Terminal Station, MSETCL, Padghe
  • Coordinator : Ms. S. R Nandurkar
  • Class : BE Final year ( BE Div A & B)
  • Total no of students : 137
  • Total no of staff : 04
Summary : The Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) built a 1,500 MW HVDC link between the cities of Chandrapur and Padghe (near Mumbai) – the first HVDC transmission link to Mumbai. The converter terminals were constructed by ABB (Sweden and India) and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) of India. The 500 kV Chandrapur – Padghe HVDC Bipole feeds Mumbai on the west coast with 1,500 MW from a thermal power generation plant located near Chandrapur in the eastern part of Maharashtra State 752 km away. The link helps to stabilize the Maharashtra grid, increasing power flow on the existing 400 kV AC lines while minimizing total line losses. Mr Sunil Shenava Deputy Executive engineer has briefed the students on the visit days. ±500 KV HVDC Padghe Plant Specification:

500 KV HVDC Padghe Plant Specification:
Commissioning Year 1999
Power Rating 1,500 MW
No. of Poles 2
AC Voltage 400 kV (both ends)
DC Voltage ±500 kV
Length of Overhead DC Line 752 km
Main Reason for Choosing HVDC Long distance, network stability, environmental concerns

privacy-policy-2.title: Privacy Policy
privacy-policy-2.html:
Privacy Statement

At A C Patil College of Engineering, we are committed to safeguarding and preserving the privacy of our visitors. You may visit our website without revealing any personal information wherever permissible. Certain transactions may require submission of personal information like profile updates and certain databases. Information that you provide when you communicate with us by any means. We will not sell, swap or rent, or otherwise disclose to any third party any personal information for commercial purpose and such information will be utilized only for the purpose stated. To accomplish such purpose we may disclose the information to our employees, consultants and other concerned having a genuine need to know the information.
On occasion we include links to third parties on this website. Where we provide a link it does not mean that we endorse or approve that site’s policy towards visitor privacy. You should review their privacy policy before sending them any personal data.
Our web server may record the numerical Internet Protocol (IP) address of the computer you are using, Information about your browser and operating system, date and time of access and page which linked you to our website. This information may be used to administer and improve our website and to generate aggregate statistical reports and such like purposes.

Use of Cookies

Cookies provide information regarding the computer used by a visitor. We may use cookies where appropriate to gather information about your computer in order to assist us in improving our website. We may gather information about your general internet use by using the cookie. Where used, these cookies are downloaded to your computer and stored on the computer’s hard drive. Such information will not identify you personally. It is statistical data. This statistical data does not identify any personal details whatsoever you can adjust the settings on your computer to decline any cookies if you wish. This can easily be done by activating the reject cookies setting on your computer. Our advertisers may also use cookies, over which we have no control. Such cookies (if used) would be downloaded once you click on advertisements on our website.

Use of Your Information

We use the information that we collect from you to provide our services to you. In addition to this we may use the information for one or more of the following purposes:

  • To provide information to you that you request from us relating to our products or services.
  • To provide information to you relating to other products that may be of interest to you. Such additional information will only be provided where you have consented to receive such information.
  • To inform you of any changes to our website, services or goods and products.

If you have previously purchased goods or services from us we may provide to you details of similar goods or services, or other goods and services, that you may be interested in.

Where your consent has been provided in advance we may allow selected third parties to use your data to enable them to provide you with information regarding unrelated goods and services which we believe may interest you. Where such consent has been provided it can be withdrawn by you at any time.

Storing your Personal Data

In operating our website it may become necessary to transfer data that we collect from you to locations outside of the Indian Subcontinent for processing and storing. By providing your personal data to us, you agree to this transfer, storing or processing. We do our utmost to ensure that all reasonable steps are taken to make sure that your data is treated stored securely.

Unfortunately the sending of information via the internet is not totally secure and on occasion such information can be intercepted. We cannot guarantee the security of data that you choose to send us electronically, sending such information is entirely at your own risk.

Contact Us

Please do not hesitate to contact us regarding any matter relating to this Privacy Policy at enquiry@acpce.org or write to us at A C Patil College of Engineering, Plot No. 17, Sion-Panvel Expressway, Opp. Kharghar Railway Station, Sector 4, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai – 410 210, Maharashtra, India.

This privacy policy may be revised/modified/amended at any point of time at the sole discretion of the A C Patil College of Engineering.

Objectives of IQAC

Objectives of IQAC
  • To develop a system for conscious, consistent and catalytic action to improve the academic and administrative performance of the institution.
  • To promote measures for institutional functioning towards quality enhancement through internalization of quality culture and institutionalization of best practices
Functions of IQAC
  1. Development and application of quality benchmarks
  2. Parameters for various academic and administrative activities of the institution.
  3. Facilitating the creation of a learner-centric environment conducive to quality education and faculty maturation to adopt the required knowledge and technology for participatory teaching and learning process.
  4. Collection and analysis of feedback from all stakeholders on quality-related institutional processes.
  5. Dissemination of information on various quality parameters to all stakeholders.
  6. Organization of inter and intra institutional workshops, seminars on quality related themes and promotion of quality circles.
  7. Documentation of the various programmes/activities leading to quality improvement.
  8. Acting as a nodal agency of the Institution for coordinating quality-related activities, including adoption and dissemination of best practices.
  9. Development and maintenance of institutional database through MIS for the purpose of maintaining /enhancing the institutional quality. i) Periodical conduct of Academic and Administrative Audit and its follow-up j) Preparation and submission of the Annual Quality Assurance Report (AQAR) as per guidelines and parameters of NAAC.
Strategies of IQAC
  1. Ensuring timely, efficient and progressive performance of academic, administrative and financial tasks.
  2. Relevant and quality academic/ research programmes.
  3. Equitable access to and affordability of academic programmes for various sections of society.
  4. Optimization and integration of modern methods of teaching and learning.
  5. The credibility of assessment and evaluation process.
  6. Ensuring the adequacy, maintenance and proper allocation of support structure and services.
  7. Sharing of research findings and networking with other institutions in India and abroad.
Benefits of IQAC
  1. Ensure clarity and focus on institutional functioning towards quality enhancement.
  2. Ensure internalization of the quality culture.
  3. Ensure enhancement and coordination among various activities of the institution and institutionalize all good practices.
  4. Provide a sound basis for decision-making to improve institutional functioning.
  5. Act as a dynamic system for quality changes in HEIs
  6. Build an organized methodology of documentation and internal communication.

capability-enhancement-and-development-s.html:
Capability Enhancement And Development Schemes

Career Counseling

It is aimed at helping the students to determine their strengths, values, and interests in order to make choices regarding their career. The college career guidance and placement cell offers resources, events, job postings throughout the year.

Career Counseling Activities

  • 1. A seminar on “Career in Java” on 20th January 2017, by Squad Infotech.
  • 2. A seminar on “Cyber Security and Penetration Testing” on 8th February 2017, by ICE Technology Lab, Kharghar.
  • 3. An orientation program by Siemens on “Opportunities in the field of Industrial Automation”, on 14th March 2018.

Guidance for Competitive Examinations

Numerous competitive examinations in India and abroad are conducted for entrance into post graduate professional courses as well as for securing services in the government. The guiding sessions for preparing these competition exams are conducted.
A seminar on “Career and Admissions to PG Courses in Abroad”, by Zep Consultant on 15th February 2018.

Soft Skill Development

The focus of this activity is to develop a wide variety of soft skills amongst the students such as communication skills, group discussions, persuasion skills, presentation skills, critical and creative thinking, etc.
A seminar on “Aptitude and Softskills” by Profound Edutech on 8th February 2018.

Bridge Course

The objective of this activity is to help the students to catch up with the pace and nature of academics in engineering courses.
A workshop on “Applications of Process Control using Lab VIEW”, on 22nd and 23rd February 2017, By Department of Instrumentation Engineering, A. C. Patil College of Engineering, Kharghar.

Personal Counselling

Personal counselling helps to increase self-confidence, improve relationships, solve problems, achieve educational goals, and make good decisions for emotional, intellectual, physical, and spiritual well-being. At our institute, we have facility of in-house mentoring by the faculty. Also experts from reputed counselling organization are invited for counselling of our students.
Counseling sessions conducted for the students by the faculties.

Yoga and Meditation

Yoga and meditation used as a healthcare tool for healthy living. Practicing yoga improves balance, endurance, flexibility, and strength, while meditation helps keep the mind sharp, relieves stress and anxiety, and can strengthen the immune system. Regular yoga sessions are conducted at the institute for students as well as faculty.
Sahaja Yoga and Meditation program conducted by Dr. Alok and Mrs. Gadge, on 25th of July 2016 , in the Seminar Hall 506.

placement-message.title: Placement Message
placement-message.html:
Message To Students

Rules for Group Discussion

Dos and Don’ts

Dos and Don’ts for Group Discussion

  • Take time to organize your thoughts. Think of what you are going to say.
  • Seek clarification if you have any doubts regarding the subject.
  • Don't start speaking until you have clearly understood and analyzed the subject.
  • Work out various strategies to help you make an entry: initiate the discussion or agree with someone else's point and then move onto express your views.
  • Opening the discussion is not the only way of gaining attention and recognition. If you do not give valuable insights during the discussion, all your efforts of initiating the discussion will be in vain.
  • Your body language says a lot about you - your gestures and mannerisms are more likely to reflect your attitude than what you say.
  • Language skills are important only to the effect as to how you get your points across clearly and fluently.
  • Be assertive not dominating; maintain eye contact with all the group members. Try to maintain a balanced tone in your discussion and analysis.
  • Put points firmly and always try to get others support too.
  • Most important don't wait for your turn to speak when discussion is on. Interrupt politely if you want to put forward your points
  • Don't lose your cool if anyone says anything you object to. The key is to stay objective: Don't take the discussion personally.
  • Always be polite: Try to avoid using extreme phrases like: `I strongly object' or `I disagree'. Instead try phrases like: `I would like to share my views on…' or `One difference between your point and mine…' or "I beg to differ with you"
  • If you find that the discussion is going off-track then never lose an opportunity to bring it back to stream this is the best point to score max.
  • Brush up on your leadership skills; motivate the other members of the team to speak (this surely does not mean that the only thing that you do in the GD is to say "let us hear what the young lady with the blue scarf has to say," or "Raghu, let us hear your views" - Essentially be subtle), and listen to their views. Be receptive to others' opinions and do not be abrasive or aggressive.
  • If you have a group of like-minded friends, you can have a mock group discussion where you can learn from each other through giving and receiving feedback.

Best scoring points are: 1. Initiation of discussion. 2. Always keeping/trying to keep discussion on track. 3. Conclusion on time. 4. Your capability to keep yourself cool and listen as well as putting your points.

Be a Leader:  GD basically means searching your team player, leadership, communication capability. Apart from the above points, the panel will also judge team members for their alertness and presence of mind, problem-solving abilities, ability to work as a team without alienating certain members, and creativity.

Personal Interview

Interviews

Interviews - do’s and don’ts

An interview is a discussion between you and an employer to find out if you can do the job. It’s your chance to make a good impression. However, there are certain rules you should follow in interviews

General Interview Tips Do:

  • Dress smartly, look bright and attentive, and speak clearly and confidently. Don't forget that in the first few minutes only 7% of the interviewer's opinion of you is formed by what you say - the rest is judged on how you look, act and sound.
  • Turn off your mobile phone: treat the interviewers with respect and give them your undivided attention.
  • Prepare answers for the main questions - for example, why do you want the job, what are your strengths and weaknesses, what are the main tasks in this job? Make about three or four points in each answer.
  • Before going to an Interview get the Job description through Training and Placement Office or through their Website. This helps you to relate your skills and background to the position throughout the interview
  • Clarify questions. Be sure you answered the questions the employer really asked.
  • Conduct yourself professionally. Be aware of what your body language is saying. Smile, make eye contact, don't slouch and maintain composure.
  • Anticipate tough questions. Prepare in advance so you can turn apparent weaknesses into strengths.
  • Listen. This is probably the most important ability of all. Concentrate on the employer's words, and also on the tone and body language, this helps you to understand and how a hiring authority thinks.

Don't:

  • Don't answer vague questions. Rather than answering questions in vague get the employer to be more specific and then respond.
  • Never interrupt the employer don’t not lie and don’t argue.
  • Don’t make answers too long nor answer questions with a simple "yes" or "no." Answer the questions in short whenever possible.

Closing the Interview:

  • After you have finished your questions, you will probably hear a comment similar to, "Well, if you don't have anything else, that should be all for today. Thanks for coming." This is an opportune time to make a strong close by summarizing your qualifications and expressing your interest in the position.
  • If you feel that the interview went well and you would like to take the next step, express your interest to the hiring authority.
  • Do not be discouraged if no definite offer is made or specific salary discussed. The interviewer will probably want to communicate with the office first, or interview other applicants, before making a decision.
  • Make sure you have clarified / answered the following two questions during the interview. "Why are you interested in the company?" and "What can you offer to the company?"
  • Express thanks for the interviewer's time and consideration.

uba.title: UBA
uba.html:
Unnat Bharat Abhiyan UBA

(Ministry of Education, Government of India)

A.C. Patil College of Engineering has established Unnat Bharat Abhiyan (UBA) which is working under Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India (GoI) with the vision to involve Professionals and Higher Educational Institutions in the developmental process of rural areas to which sustainable development & better quality of experiential learning among students.

Our Vision & Mission

Our Vision

Unnat Bharat Abhiyan is inspired by the vision of transformational change in rural development processes by leveraging knowledge institutions to help build the architecture of an Inclusive India.

Our Mission

The Mission of Unnat Bharat Abhiyan is to enable higher educational institutions to work with the people of rural India in identifying development challenges and evolving appropriate solutions for accelerating sustainable growth. It also aims to create a virtuous cycle between society and an inclusive academic system by providing knowledge and practices for emerging professions and to upgrade the capabilities of both the public and the private sectors in responding to the development needs of rural India.

Goals

  • To build an understanding of the development agenda within institutes of Higher Education and an institutional capacity and training relevant to national needs, especially those of rural India.
  • To re-emphasize the need for field work, stake-holder interactions and design for societal objectives as the basis of higher education.
  • To stress on rigorous reporting and useful outputs as central to developing new professions.
  • To provide rural India and regional agencies with access to the professional resources of the institutes of higher education, especially those that have acquired academic excellence in the field of science, engineering and technology, and management.
  • To improve development outcomes as a consequence of this research. To develop new professions and new processes to sustain and absorb the outcomes of research.
  • To foster a new dialogue within the larger community on science, society and the environment and to develop a sense of dignity and collective destiny.

Under the UBA program all Participating Institutes are adopting a cluster of five villages in consultation with Districts Collectors. A letter in this regards has already been circulated to Districts Collectors by MHRD. A. C. Patil College of Engineering, Kharghar, Navi-Mumbai adopted a cluster of 5 villages namely:

  • 3. The readers should check the book thoroughly for missing pages, chapters, pictures etc., while borrowing the book.
  • 4. No book in damaged condition will be accepted from the reader. Mutilated or spoiled books will have to be replaced by the borrower.
  • 5. Books issued will not be accepted back on the same day.
  • 6. Reader can claim books (reserve) already issued, at the circulation counter.
  • 7. Loss of book must be reported immediately. Late fees, if any, will be charged till the loss of book is reported. If the original library book is returned after reporting it lost, the fine will be calculated till the date of its return.
  • 8. For the rules for replacement of lost book kindly contact the Circulation Section.
  • 9. Books are reissued only if there are no claims.
  • 10. The borrowing facility can be withdrawn or restricted in case of misbehavior or misuse of the library.

Issue/Return Timing

  • Monday – Saturday: 09.30 AM – 05.30 PM

Reference Section

The Library has reference section consisting of Reference books, Encyclopedias, Dictionaries, Directories, Handbooks, Technical data, Atlases, Bibliographies, CD –ROMs etc. Readers may approach the Reference section for information or any assistance in the use of the various Collections and Services. Users can also search the books using intranet based WebOPAC facility.

about-library.title: About Library
about-library.html:
Collection

The Library has developed an excellent collection of books, journals and non-book material covering the principle fields of interest in engineering streams like Electronics, Computer Science, Mechanical, Electrical, Information Technology, Instrumentation, Electronics and Telecommunication and Management etc. The library has a good collection of Project reports and rare Books. It maintains separate collections of Reference Books and Bound volumes of journals.

Particulars Available
Volumes 40210
Titles 12874
National/International Journals 50
E-Journals 738
E-Books 4166
Multimedia CD 2118

Library Rules

  • 1. All the students entering the Library shall keep their bags and other personal belongings at the entrance. Staff / Students will first sign in the Register at the Counter, before being allowed to approach Circulation Counter.
  • 2. Only notebooks and the Library books will be allowed inside.
  • 3. All the readers are advised not to leave their valuables at the Check Point. Library is not responsible for any loss of personal belongings.
  • 4. I Card should be compulsory for entering into the library.
  • 5. Books Borrowed should be protected from RAIN, DUST, INSECT, etc.
  • 6. Books removed from the shelves, if not required further, should be kept on the table nearest to them. Please do not try to shelve them yourself. Please remember that a book misplaced is a book lost.
  • 7. Newspaper should be folded properly after reading and kept back in the designated place.
  • 8. Readers should not deface, mark, cut, mutilate or damage library resources in any way. If anyone is found doing so, he will be charged the full replacement cost of the resource.
  • 9. All the students are required to bring their recent passport size photograph while applying for Library membership.
  • 10. All students are allowed to borrow 3 books at a time for a period of 7 days.
  • 11. Faculty, staff going on long leaves like vacation will have to return all borrowed material before leaving Mumbai.
  • 12. All the students who want to return the books issued on their names are advised to wait until the books are shown as cancelled against their names.
  • 13. There will be a fine of Rs. 2.00 per book per day.
  • 14. Students are advised not to issue Books to others on their names.
  • 15. Reference Documents like Dictionary, Encyclopedia, Year Books, Journals (Loose & Bound), Project Reports, Handbooks will not be issued out.
  • 16. Borrower must make good the loss by replacing library material with same or latest edition. In case of non-availability of material, then the actual cost of the book / material or Rs. 400.00, whichever is higher will be recovered by the borrower.
  • 17. Conversation and discussion disturbs library ambiance. Therefore, all are requested to maintain dignified silence.
  • 18. Smoking is not permitted in the Library.
  • 19. All users are requested to keep their mobiles in silent mode.
  • 20. Beverages and Eatables are not allowed inside the library.
  • 21. No photograph of the Library shall be taken without the prior permission of the Librarian.
  • 22. Demand and suggestion slips are available at the circulation desk for your use.

Location

The Central Library is located on the third floor with an area of over 630 sq. mts. The distribution of services and resources in the Library is indicated below:
  • 1. Property Counter
  • 2. Reference Section and Reading Hall
  • 3. Journals / Magazines (Periodicals) Section
  • 4. Issue / Return Section
  • 5. Newspaper Section
  • 6. Project Reports
  • 7. Librarian’s Office
  • 8. Multimedia Section

Library Working Hours

The primary mission of the library is to support the educational and research programs of the institute by providing physical and intellectual access to information, consistent with the present and the anticipated educational and research functions of the institute. “The Master of Management Studies, popularly abbreviated as MMS, is the two-year, full-time post graduate program of ACPCE. The program is affiliated to the University of Mumbai, and also approved by AICTE and Government of Maharashtra. This MMS course is equivalent or similar to MBA courses elsewhere”.

Our Vision & Mission

Our Vision

To develop competent management professionals that meet the needs of industries and society.

Our Mission

  • Imparting comprehensive managerial knowledge through qualified faculty and infrastructure.
  • To encourage interactions with industries, institutions and professional bodies for continuous improvement.
  • To nurture responsive ethical managers sensitive to environment and society.

Objectives & Outcomes

Objectives

  • To focus on passion for quality, nurture creative and resourceful minds who think big, think fast , think ahead with humility , compassion and concern for all.
  • To develop individuals who are morally, spiritually, intellectually, socially and culturally well informed to keep pace with the changing business world/scenario.

Outcomes

  • Students Our holistic approach education trains the individual through a learning process that foresees the creativity and encourages execuence in all their endeavors.
  • Faculty To engage in consequential research for development of faculty through TOTAL’S (training of trainers) and providing enriching , flexible and challenging work environment.

Syllabus

First Year

Second Year

Message From HOD

In this highly competitive and dynamic business environment, there is a pressing need for highly qualified business leaders and entrepreneurs.  Our Master of Management Studies (MMS)  program is designed to develop future leaders who are equipped with the skills, knowledge and vision to navigate the complex and dynamic business environment. Our curriculum blends theoretical concepts with practical applications through case studies, projects, internships, and industry interactions ensuring that our students gain a comprehensive understanding of business management. We offer MMS course that cover essential areas such as finance, marketing, operations, human resources, and systems. Our faculty comprises experienced professionals and academicians who are dedicated to providing high-quality education and mentorship

At ACPCE, we believe in the holistic development of our students. We encourage participation in extracurricular activities, leadership programs, and community service, which help to build well-rounded individuals who are not only skilled managers but also responsible citizens.

Prof. Abhijeet Vijay Salunke

MBA Finance

student-association.title: Student Association
student-association.html:
Computer Society of India

Formed in 1965, the CSI has been instrumental in guiding the Indian IT industry down the right path since its formative years. Today, the CSI has 70 chapters all over India, 358 student branches, and more than 90,000 members, including India’s most famous IT industry leaders, brilliant scientists and dedicated academicians. Now, you have the opportunity to be a part of this distinguished fraternity too. The mission of the CSI is to facilitate research, knowledge sharing, learning and career enhancement for all categories of IT professionals, while simultaneously inspiring and nurturing new entrants into the industry and helping them to integrate into the IT community. Information Technology Department has student association CSI-ACPCE active under CSI professional body. Various technical activities are organized for students under the banner of CSI-ACPCE to improve their skills.
