student-activities.title: Student Activities
student-activities.html:
Department of Information Technology

Alumni engagement on “Real Time Job Market”

The Department of Information Technology organized an alumni engagement session on “Real Time Job Market” on 3rd October 2025. Alumni shared valuable insights into current industry trends, recruitment practices, and the evolving skills required to succeed in today’s competitive environment.

The interactive discussion helped students gain a practical understanding of job market dynamics, preparing them to align their academic learning with real‑world opportunities and career growth.

Session on, "Achieving Value Proposition Fit" & "Business Fit"

The Department of Information Technology organized a session on “Achieving Value Proposition Fit” and “Business Fit” on 25th September 2025, led by Dr. Nagendra Pratap Singh from Perpetual Gravity Labs. The objective was to help students understand how to align a product’s value proposition with customer needs while ensuring a sustainable and viable business model.

The session provided practical insights into bridging innovation with market expectations, encouraging students to think critically about product relevance, customer satisfaction, and long‑term business success.

Seminar on “The Blueprint of Success for Engineers”

The Department of Information Technology hosted an inspiring seminar on “The Blueprint of Success for Engineers” on 22nd September 2025, featuring Mr. Raghvan Koli, renowned author and motivational speaker. He shared practical strategies for resilience, adaptability, and lifelong learning, while highlighting the importance of communication, networking, and global exposureThe interactive session energized students, offering clear guidance on balancing technical expertise with soft skills and motivating them to pursue excellence with confidence in today’s competitive world

Workshop on “Full Stack Web Development”

A workshop on Full Stack Web Development was conducted on 18th September to equip students with foundational knowledge of front-end and back-end technologies, databases, and integration techniques. Mr. Mahimkar guided participants through the process of designing, developing, and deploying complete web applications. The session fostered problem-solving skills and prepared students for career opportunities in software development, bridging academic learning with industry practices.

Engineer’s Day

The Department of Information Technology CelebtratedThe  Engineer’s Day to honor the contributions of engineers and inspire students to embrace innovation and problem-solving. The celebration emphasized the importance of engineering in nation-building and encouraged students to uphold professional values while pursuing excellence in their academic and career journeys.

Workshop on “Cyber Security”

The Department of Information Technology organized a workshop on “Cyber Security” on 11 September 2025, conducted by Mr. Sumit Utekar, Cybersecurity & Cloud Computing Trainer. The objective of the workshop was to raise student awareness about fundamental cybersecurity concepts, emerging threats, and best practices for safeguarding digital assets. The session also aimed to prepare participants to adopt secure digital habits while introducing them to potential career opportunities in the field of cybersecurity.

Alumni engagement on “How to Apply for Higher Studies Abroad”

The Department of Information Technology conducted a session on “How to Apply for Higher Studies Abroad” on 08 September 2025, featuring Ms. Sakshi Shinde as the speaker. The purpose of the session was to provide students with practical guidance on pursuing international education, covering university selection, application procedures, documentation requirements, and scholarship opportunities. Ms. Shinde shared her personal experiences and offered valuable insights into financial planning and cultural adaptation, which were further enriched through an interactive Q&A segment. The session successfully enhanced awareness of global academic pathways, strengthened alumni-student connections, and motivated participants to confidently pursue higher studies abroad. Overall, the event was impactful and well-received, reinforcing the importance of alumni-led initiatives in supporting academic and professional aspirations.

Seminar on “Career Guidance”

The Department of Information Technology organized a seminar on “Career Guidance” on 8th August 2025. The session was conducted by Mr. Vicky Mulchandani, who shared his expertise and insights with the students.

The objective of the seminar was to create awareness among students about various career opportunities and options for higher studies. The speaker emphasized the importance of informed decision-making, skill development, and continuous learning in shaping a successful professional journey.

The seminar proved to be highly beneficial, offering students valuable guidance on planning their future careers and exploring avenues for advanced education.

Hands-on Workshop on ‘Power BI Technology’

The Department of Information Technology organized a hands-on workshop on “Power BI Technology” on 2nd April 2025. The session was conducted by Ms. Namrata Modi from the All India Institute of Integrated Technical Studies, Pinnacle Technology, Kharghar.

The objective of the workshop was to empower participants with the skills and knowledge required to effectively utilize Power BI for data analysis, reporting, and visualization. The session provided practical exposure to key features of Power BI, enabling students to understand how to transform raw data into meaningful insights through interactive dashboards and reports.

The workshop proved to be highly beneficial, equipping participants with essential competencies in business intelligence tools and preparing them to apply data-driven decision-making in academic and professional contexts.

Poster Presentation Competition

The Department of  Information Technology organized a Poster Presentation Competition on 28th March 2025. The event was graced by the presence of Dr. D. S. Marathe, Head of the Department of Electronics & Telecommunication, and Dr. A. R. Sonule, Associate Professor in the Computer Department.

The competition aimed to provide students with an excellent platform for presenting innovative ideas and testing creative solutions. It encouraged participants to showcase their knowledge, analytical skills, and research aptitude in both hardware and software domains.

A total of 21 entries were received in the Hardware category and 17 entries in the Software category, reflecting enthusiastic participation and diverse perspectives from students. The event successfully fostered innovation, collaboration, and critical thinking among participants.

Session on “Emerging Trends and Applications of Generative AI”

The Department of Information Technology organized a session on “Emerging Trends and Applications of Generative AI” on 21st March 2025. The session was conducted by Mr. HemantKumar Wani, Principal Architect (GenAI) at Persistent Systems, Bangalore.

The objective of the session was to provide students with insights into the rapidly evolving field of Generative AI. Mr. Wani highlighted the latest industry trends, practical applications, and the transformative potential of GenAI across various domains. The session emphasized how Generative AI is reshaping innovation, problem-solving, and future career opportunities in technology.

The program proved to be highly informative and engaging, equipping students with valuable knowledge about emerging technologies and inspiring them to explore advanced applications of AI in their academic and professional pursuits.

Session on “Problem Solving and Ideation Workshop”

The Department of Information Technology organized a session on “Problem Solving and Ideation Workshop” on 13th March 2025. The workshop was conducted by Mr. Ganesh Iyer, a Behavioral Trainer, Start-Up Mentor, and Learning & Development Consultant from Hyderabad.

The objective of the session was to equip students with practical approaches to problem-solving and ideation. Mr. Iyer guided participants on how to define core challenges, identify root causes validated through data or stakeholder input, and evaluate and shortlist innovative ideas. The workshop also emphasized the importance of collaboration and communication in the ideation process and provided strategies for establishing actionable plans.

The session proved to be highly insightful, enabling students to develop structured thinking, enhance teamwork, and gain confidence in applying creative solutions to real-world challenges.

Workshop on “Internet of Things (IoT)”

The Department of Information Technology organized a workshop on “Internet of Things (IoT)” on 22nd January 2025. The session was conducted by student presenters:

  • Sarthak Shinde (BE IT)
  • Prajwal Sankpal (BE Computer Engineering)
  • Aditya Pawar (SE Computer Engineering)
  • Dinesh Yendluri (BE IoT)

The objective of the workshop was to introduce students to the fundamentals of IoT and provide hands-on learning experiences. The topics covered included:

  • Basics of Arduino
  • Arduino IDE
  • Working with sensors
  • Connecting a PS5 Controller to Arduino using a USB Host Shield

The workshop offered participants practical exposure to IoT concepts and tools, fostering innovation and technical skills. It served as an excellent platform for students to gain insights into real-world applications of IoT and strengthen their foundation in emerging technologies.

Workshop on “Higher Education Abroad”

The Department of Information Technology organized an online workshop on “Higher Education Abroad” on 25th October 2024. The session was conducted by Mr. Yash Hankare, Penetration Tester at Cyber Node, Perth, Western Australia.

The objective of the workshop was to provide students with valuable insights into pursuing higher education opportunities overseas. Mr. Hankare shared his experiences and expertise, guiding students on the academic pathways, skill requirements, and global prospects associated with studying abroad.

The workshop offered an excellent platform for students to understand the scope of international education and prepare themselves for future academic and professional endeavors.

Student Development Program on “React JS Fundamentals”

The Department of Information Technology organized a Student Development Program on “React JS Fundamentals” on 5th October 2024. The session was conducted by Ms. Charu Saraswat, Business Manager and Software Developer, who shared her expertise with the participants.

The objective of the program was to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamentals of React JS, a widely used JavaScript library for building user interfaces. The speaker explained key concepts, practical applications, and industry relevance, enabling students to strengthen their technical foundation and enhance their employability skills.

The program proved to be highly informative and beneficial, equipping students with valuable knowledge to pursue further learning and career opportunities in web development.

Poster Presentation Competition

The Department of Information Technology organized a Poster Presentation Competition on 4th October 2024. The event was inaugurated and guided by Dr. Mahi Khemchandani, Head of the Department of Information Technology(Saraswati College of Engg.).

The competition aimed to provide students with an excellent platform to present innovative ideas and explore creative solutions. It served as a space for testing new concepts, encouraging critical thinking, and fostering research-oriented learning among participants.

The initiative was highly engaging and offered students an opportunity to showcase their knowledge, creativity, and problem-solving skills in a collaborative environment.

Seminar on “Career Guidance”

The Department of Information Technology organized a seminar on “Career Guidance” on 1st October 2024. The session was conducted by Mr. Vicky Mulchandani, who shared his expertise and insights with the students.

The objective of the seminar was to create awareness among students about various career opportunities and options for higher studies. The speaker emphasized the importance of informed decision-making, skill development, and continuous learning in shaping a successful professional journey.

The seminar proved to be highly beneficial, offering students valuable guidance on planning their future careers and exploring avenues for advanced education.

Webinar titled “Kickstart Your Career in Cyber Security”

The Department of Information Technology successfully conducted a webinar titled “Kickstart Your Career in Cyber Security” on 24th September 2024. The session was graced by Ms. Swati Shirsat, Founder & CEO of Techverse Upskill E-Learning, who served as the distinguished speaker.

The primary objective of the webinar was to provide students with an understanding of the fundamentals of cyber security and to highlight the diverse career opportunities available in this rapidly growing field. The event offered valuable insights into industry trends, essential skills, and pathways for building a successful career in cyber security.

The initiative was well-received by participants and contributed significantly to raising awareness among students about the importance of cyber security in today’s digital era.

Session on “Accelerators/Incubation-Opportunities for Students and Faculties-Early Stage Entrepreneurs”

The student council of Information Technology in association with CSI had organized session on “Accelerators/Incubation-Opportunities for students and faculties-Early Stage Entrepreneurs” on 26 August 2024 for our students and faculties. Dr. Pranita Pathak Assistant Vice President (Program) SINE IITB and Dr. Priyanka Majumdar Assistant Manager (Programs) SINE IITB was the speakers. The objective of the session was to make students and faculties aware about the Incubation Opportunities and Entrepreneurship

Poster presentation competition

Dr. Avinash Sonule, Computer dept, ACPCE, Dr. Jayprabha Terdale, EXTC dept. ACPCE was the judge. Final year and third year student has enthusiastically participated and showcased their talent

The Objective of session was to Understand the root cause of a problem, Quickly generate ideas to solve it, Evaluate the ideas to ensure they’re robust and Make a plan to test or implement the solution·

Bhole who enlightened the participants about the importance of such training programs and how such programs helps in developing applications in industry. Principal Dr. V. N. Understood the problems, solutions, Reasons for failure of Start up and Success Features of Entrepreneurship.

The student council of Information Technology in association with CSI had organized a seminar on ” Career Opportunity after Engineering (GATE /PSUs /Private sectors)” on 29th August 2023. Overview:

B.E. Aeronautical Engineering at ACPCE Kharghar is a comprehensive program that delves into the intricate world of Air Carriers, Helicopters, Drones, Missiles, and Both Commercial and Non-commercial Airplanes. This program encompasses Planning, Design, Structural Analysis, Aerodynamics, Propulsion, and Flight Mechanics. Our curriculum is engineered for holistic student development through Case Studies, Simulations, Group Discussions, and Hands-on Training. This course paves the way for bright careers in prestigious space research centers, Aeronautical Establishments, and Aviation Industries.

Curriculum:

  • Aircraft Control and Guidance
  • Spacecraft Engineering
  • Aerodynamics

Introduction

The Internet of things (IoT) is a system of interrelated computing devices, mechanical and digital machines provided with unique identifiers (UIDs) and the ability to transfer data over a network without requiring human-to-human or human-to-computer interaction. Cybersecurity is the protection of computer systems and networks from the theft of or damage to their hardware, software, or electronic data, as well as from the disruption or misdirection of the services they provide. Blockchain technology can be used to protect systems, and devices from attacks , blockchain security means that there is no longer a centralized authority controlling the network and verifying the data going through it Computer Science & Engineering (Internet of things and Cyber security including Block chain technology) undergraduate engineering course has been started by the institute from the academic year July 2020 with the intake capacity of 60 seats.

  1. Engineering knowledge : Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering Problems.
  2. Problem Analysis : Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1 to WK4)
  3. Design/Development Solutions : Design/Development of Solutions: Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5)
  4. Conduct investigations of complex problems: Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8).
  5. The engineer Tool Usage: Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering & IT tools, including prediction and modelling recognizing their limitations to solve complex engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6)
  6. The Engineer and The World: Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7).

  9. Communication : Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences
  10. Project management and finance : Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
  11. Life-long learning : Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8)

Message From HOD

The Department of Mechanical Engineering came into being in the year 2013 and the first batch of Mechanical Engineers graduated in the year 2017. Our departments has a team of highly qualified and experienced faculty, excellent infrastructure and lab facilities. Mechanical Engineering is versatile and evergreen branch of engineering. Mechanical engineer can work in various specialized area like automotive system, aerospace engineering, design engineering, dynamic system and control, power plant engineering, etc. The hands-on-practice at Mechanical Engineering departments is contributing strongly in automobile, thermal, design and manufacturing areas. Regular interaction with industry through collaborative projects, course requirements and general discussions on advancements in technological aspects develop an environment closer to the practical essence of engineering. Regular activities are arranged and encouraged in the departments for indigenous product development, skills enhancement and interdisciplinary interactions. The department has laboratory and workshop facilities with modern sophisticated equipment’s to carry out related to Mechanical Engineering. The faculty actively participates in sponsored research and consultancy work. We encourage our UG students to participate in these research efforts through mini & major projects. Graduates from our departments are employed in premier manufacturing Engineering, Automobile industries, and a good number pursues higher studies in renowned universities abroad.

Dr.-Girish P. Deshmukh

  6. The Engineer and The World: Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7).
  7. Ethics : Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws.(WK9)
  8. Individual and Collaborative Team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams.
  9. Communication : Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences
  10. Project management and finance : Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
  11. Life-long learning : Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8)

Message From HOD

The Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering is one of the most dynamic departments at the institute. It equips students with the skills to apply their knowledge effectively in multidisciplinary teams. The department also fosters leadership and technical expertise, emphasizing the importance of ethical engineering practices. Its goal is not only to make students technically proficient and knowledgeable but also to cultivate wisdom, making them more responsible and well-rounded individuals. The department is committed to serving society and humanity. We are pleased to see that a significant number of our students are placed in core companies and IT sectors, with many also pursuing higher education abroad.

Dr. Deepak S. Marathe

(BE, ME, PhD Tech.)

Introduction Electrical Engineering

The Department of Electrical Engineering at ACPCE is committed to providing students with the latest and most advanced technical knowledge in the field of Electrical Engineering. The department boasts a team of experienced and highly qualified faculty members who are dedicated to guiding students in their academic and professional growth. The department is equipped with modern classrooms and state-of-the-art laboratories, ensuring that students receive practical, hands-on experience. Additionally, the department’s library houses an extensive collection of books and resources, supporting students in their learning journey.

Program Educational Objectives(PEOs)

PEO1 : To apply concepts of Electrical Engineering using modern tools for the design and analysis of systems.
PEO2 : To communicate and contribute in research and development by providing innovative solutions considering social values.
PEO3 : To use professional and personal skills to succeed in multi-disciplinary activities.

Program Specific Outcomes(PSOs)

PSO1: To create professionals through the use of commercial tools, expert talks, workshops, industrial visits, participation in technical events, and in-plant training.
PSO2: To inculcate a nation-first consciousness through cultural, social, and environmental activities

Program Outcomes(POs)
  1. Engineering knowledge : Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop to the solution of complex engineering Problems.
  2. Problem Analysis : Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1 to WK4)
  3. Design/Development Solutions : Design/Development of Solutions: Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design/develop systems/components/processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon, culture, society and environment as required. (WK5)
  4. Conduct investigations of complex problems: Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8).
  5. The engineer Tool Usage: Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engineering & IT tools, including prediction and modelling recognizing their limitations to solve complex engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6)
  6. The Engineer and The World: Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving complex engineering problems for its impact on sustainability with reference to economy, health, safety, legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7).
  7. Ethics : Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclusion; adhere to national & international laws.(WK9)
  8. Individual and Collaborative Team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams.
  9. Communication : Communicate effectively and inclusively within the engineering community and society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences
  10. Project management and finance : Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
  11. Life-long learning : Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change. (WK8)

Most Advanced Technical Knowledge in the field of Electrical Engineering.

Our Vision & Mission

Our Vision

To develop professionals in the field of Electrical Engineering domain having social values.

Our Mission

  • To provide fundamental and applied knowledge through qualified faculty and infrastructure.
  • To improve technical skills by industry institute interaction.
  • To provide platform for enhancing social values.

Message From HOD

The growth of a nation relies heavily on resources for industrial and agricultural development, with electrical energy being a key resource in both underdeveloped and developed countries. The generation, transmission, and distribution of electrical energy continue to grow, highlighting the vital role of electrical engineers in daily life. The Electrical Engineering undergraduate program, established in 1992 with an intake of 60, includes a recognized research center by the University of Mumbai since 2019. The department focuses on producing skilled professionals, supported by experienced faculty, staff, and necessary infrastructure. Many faculty members contribute to curriculum design and assessment at the University level. The curriculum emphasizes practical, multidisciplinary learning through projects and optional courses.

Dr. Dipti D. Patil

admission-criteria.html:
Admission Criteria

The admission procedure will be carried out as per the rules prescribed by the Directorate of Technical Education, Government of Maharashtra, including the eligibility criteria. Please visit the MAHACET website www.mahacet.org for eligibility and rules. Please click on the link to check the documents required https://acpce.ac.in/documents-required/ and https://acpce.ac.in/fees-structure/ Fee structure for admission 2025-26.

The institute every years forms committee for smooth and transparent admission process. It mainly consists of counseling team, admission team, advertisement team etc,

Counseling team helps candidate to know about admission process and inform them about various courses and fees structure of institute.

Advertisement committee prepares institute prospect, which highlights institute courses, achievements and contact details.

Admission sections take care of allotted students and complete the admission procedure.

The Institute ensures smooth induction of fresh batches at the beginning of the academic session through an orientation program. This orientation program includes a welcome to the newcomers. The presentation being scheduled where all aspect required for new comers included. The new comers are being guided by the teaching and non-teaching staff to familiarize with the formalities after admission and help them to adapt the new environment.

Fees and Reservation

The institute is self finance and its fees for given academic year is decided “Fees Regulatory Authority”. Institute adhere all the rules and regulation of “Fees Regulatory Authority”. The detail fees structure for given academic year and modes of payment are displayed on institute website and notice board. Institute also provides contact number of counseling team members to help candidate for admission related information. After document verification students are required to pay fees through DD or Online. 

Category Tuition Fees Development Fees Caution Money Deposit Other Fees
Open 100 % 100 % 100 % 100 %
OBC/EBC/SEBC/EWS 50 % 100 % 100 % 100 %
SC/ST 0 % 0 % 100 % 100 %
NT/SBC/TFWS 0 % 100 % 100 % 100 %
Institute Level and Vacant Seats 100 % 100 % 100 % 100 %
All Category 100 % 100 % 100 % 100 %

The institutes forwarding all documents of SC/ST/SBC/NT/OBC students to “Samaj Kalyan” for claiming balance fees and EBC students to state government for fees concession. Institute follows seats reservation policy for different category students as per “Pravesh Niyantran Samitee”

Admission Category

Institute is conducting admission under following three categories

2.1 CAP Seats

CAP seats include minimum 80% seats of sanction intake, lateral entry all seats of direct second year and Tuition fees waiver scheme (TFWS) seats. CAP seats are filled as per rules and regulation of DTE, Mumbai.

The following procedure is followed for admission to CAP seats,

  • Institute submit in addition of 80% seats of sanction intake seats to DTE, for admission to first year
  • Admission related information such as courses and intake, fees structure displayed on institute web site
  • Institute follows the CAP procedure as per declared by DTE website.
  • Students confirming their admission in ARC, and report to institute after final round.
1. Admission helps desk team
  • Student will report to help desk team with allotment letter and will understood procedure of admission
  • Help Desk team team will verify original documents and allotment letter
2. Fees collection team
  • Team will collect fee in form of DD or Online too.
3. Original documents collection team

Students will submit original document’s Xerox copies and soft copies in pdf form to team.

2.2 Institute Level Seats

  • Institute publishes advertisement for institute level seats admission in daily news paper.
  • Interested students submit application at institute office.
  • Institute display allotment based on choice and merit number.
  • Admitted students will have to pay institutional fees as per rules

2.3 Against Vacant Seats

  • Institute publish advertisement of vacant seats in state level news paper
  • Institute allots seats as per choices and merit number

Empowering Education with Research, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship. Powered by Technology, Faculty Excellence, Industry Collaboration, Inclusio and a Mindset of Growth.

About ACPCE

In a world bursting with limitless possibilities, it takes more than just knowledge to stand out. At the core of our ‘everything + imagination’ philosophy lies a secret to true greatness: daring to dream beyond bounds and redefining the known. It’s where innovation flourishes, paving the path to extraordinary creations!

Our Vision & Mission

Our Vision

To create skilled professionals and engineers for catering the needs of industries and society.

Our Mission

  • To provide qualified faculty and required infrastructure to impart quality education inculcating continuous learning attitude
  • To provide a platform for the interaction between academia and industry.
  • To inculcate social values and responsible attitude amongst students through co-curricular and extracurricular activities.

A comprehensive approach to education with a focus on practical application

Unlock Your Innovative Potential with the ACPCE Innovation Cell. At ACPCE, we cultivate a culture of creativity and critical thinking, providing students with the resources and support needed to tackle real-world problems. Our Innovation Cell serves as a platform for students to explore new ideas, collaborate on impactful projects, and develop groundbreaking solutions. Through mentorship, workshops, and access to cutting-edge tools, we empower the next generation of innovators to lead in technology, entrepreneurship, and beyond.

A vibrant community of engaged and accomplished scholars

Our faculty, made up of esteemed researchers, accomplished scholars, and seasoned industry professionals, bring a wealth of expertise and hands-on experience to every classroom. Their deep understanding of both theory and practice enables them to deliver a rich, relevant learning experience that prepares students for the real world. Beyond teaching, they provide personalized mentorship, guiding students through their academic journey while helping them develop essential skills for their careers. Whether through one-on-one support or collaborative projects, our faculty is dedicated to nurturing students into competent, confident professionals who are ready to make an impact in their fields.

Experience the fusion of imagination and celebration at ACPCE

AC Patil College of Engineering: A Hub Where Innovation Flourishes. Our campus is a thriving ecosystem that encourages collaboration, creativity, and a passion for learning. We emphasize a hands-on, practical approach to education, ensuring that students can apply theoretical knowledge in real-world scenarios. Our state-of-the-art classrooms and labs are designed to inspire discovery and foster intellectual growth, while our makerspaces provide the perfect setting for students to experiment, build, and bring their ideas to life. Beyond academics, ACPCE offers a vibrant campus life, with opportunities to engage in extracurricular activities, sports, and artistic endeavors, helping students develop well-rounded skills.

about-us.title: About Us
about-us.html:
About Jawahar Education Society

Jawahar Education Society, founded in 1970, is a key part of the prestigious Jawahar Group, which operates 50 schools, 3 postgraduate colleges, 3 engineering colleges, and a medical college with an 800-bed hospital in Maharashtra. The group positively impacts the lives of over 20,000 students annually. The legacy of Late Annasaheb Chudaman Patil, a passionate advocate for fundamental education and rural healthcare, serves as the inspiration behind the society’s mission.

About ACPCE

Established in 1992, ACPCE is a NAAC-accredited engineering college in Navi Mumbai, offering courses in various engineering streams. With modern infrastructure and a focus on holistic development, the college fosters student participation in academics, co-curricular, and sports activities, guided by Hon. Rohidasji Patil, Hon. Vinay Patil, and Hon. Kunal Patil.

Our Campus

Located on a sprawling 3-acre campus in Kharghar, Navi Mumbai, A. C. Patil College of Engineering (ACPCE) prides itself on its ultra-large infrastructure, providing an ideal environment for both academic and extracurricular activities. Established in 1992 by the esteemed leader, Honourable Shri Rohidasji Patil, under the aegis of Jawahar Education Society, ACPCE has risen to become a premier technical institute in the region.

From The Principal's Desk

Our main aim is to create, nurture and shape technical professionals with skills to face then ever changing social, economical and technical landscape of our country. We provide high-end undergraduate education and research opportunities in new frontiers of Engineering and Technology. We provide opportunities to the students for interaction with the experts from the industry through Guest Lectures, Industrial Visits, Vocational Training (internship).We have excellent faculty, state-of-the-art infrastructure and laboratories. Spacious campus, digital library and peaceful atmosphere ensures that learning becomes a wonderful experience.

Dr. Sawata R. Deore

(BE, ME, PhD Tech.)

Accreditation & Recognition

Our University Affiliation

The college is Affiliated to University of Mumbai Maharashtra, since 1992.

Approved by AICTE

All the Engineering and MBA programs offered by the college, have been approved by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), New Delhi, India

Recognized by Govt. of Maharashtra

All the Engineering and MBA programs offered by the college, have been Recognized by Government of Maharashtra
